title: What is heads-up poker?
content: The article explains that heads‑up poker— a one‑on‑one format—has grown in popularity because of its fast pace and strategic depth. Online platforms now offer dedicated heads‑up games and tournaments, and the 2025 National Heads‑Up Poker Championship will feature top pros and celebrities, underscoring the format’s appeal. Heads‑up poker differs from full‑ring games in that hand ranges are wider, position is crucial, and bluffing and continuation bets become more frequent. The article outlines the basic rules: in Texas Hold ’em, the dealer posts the small blind and acts first pre‑flop, while the big blind leads post‑flop; betting options include checking, calling, raising (minimum raise equals the big blind or previous raise), or folding. It also describes betting in no‑limit and limit formats, and notes that in a £5/£10 game a raise to £20 is valid. Variations covered include Texas Hold ’em, Pot‑Limit Omaha, Omaha Hi/Lo, and Stud. The author offers practical tips: play wide from the button, use 3‑bets from the big blind, employ continuation bets and bluffs, adjust ranges based on opponent tendencies, and maintain balance to avoid predictability. The piece concludes that mastering heads‑up poker requires constant adaptation, aggression, and opponent analysis, and it encourages responsible gambling practices.

title: Bachelorette-Sieger träumt vom Poker-Coup: Dayan startet ins Millionen-Event der WSOP
content: Devin Dayan, the 2024 Bachelorette winner, is competing in the €10,350 Main Event of the World Series of Poker Europe (WSOP Europe) in Rozvadov, Czech Republic, starting on Saturday at 10:35 a.m. He earned his entry by winning the BILD POKER NIGHT in December 2024. Dayan expressed excitement, stating he has been anticipating the event for weeks and is 'extremely hyped' despite some nervousness. He will begin on Day 1B, facing hundreds of opponents, with the goal of reaching the money ranks—where he would recoup his entry fee. The top prize is expected to exceed €1 million, though the path is long, requiring at least four days of play. Dayan plans to stay calm, play selectively, and rely on patience, a key strategy in extended tournaments. He has been preparing by playing poker with friends and online on GGPoker. Meanwhile, German pro Christopher Pütz advanced to Day 2 on Friday, finishing second behind the leader. A total of 304 players advanced to Day 2, which Dayan aims to achieve.

title: World Series of Poker: Poker-Thriller in Rozvadov
content: Eight players remain in the final of the €10,350 Main Event at the World Series of Poker Europe (WSOPE) in Rozvadov, Czech Republic, with the new European poker champion to be crowned starting at 17:00. German players Daniel Pidun (ranked 3rd) and Matthias Gude (far behind) both have a chance at winning the gold bracelet and a prize of €1.1 million, though Gude needs a miracle to remain competitive. The remaining players are closely matched, making every hand and mistake potentially decisive. The final table is expected to be one of the most exciting in recent years. Austrian player Max Neugebauer, the 2023 WSOPE Main Event champion, is back and could become the first player to win the event twice. All finalists have already secured €110,000 each, eliminating the risk of losing everything. Martin Kabrhel, who led after Day 3, was eliminated in 14th place. Live coverage begins at 17:00 on the 'PokerTotal' YouTube channel, hosted by Martin Pott and Markus Altkirch. Notably, this will be the final WSOPE event in Rozvadov; the next edition will be held in Prague from March 31 to April 12, 2026, at the Hilton hotel, featuring 15 bracelet events.

title: Poker-Profi aus Österreich gewinnt immer weiter
content: Klemens Roiter, a 30‑year‑old poker professional from Vienna, continues his winning streak after capturing a gold bracelet at the World Series of Poker (WSOP) in Las Vegas. On 23 August 2025 he won the 30,000‑Euro Super High Roller Warm‑up event of the European Poker Tour (EPT) in Barcelona, earning 507,000 Euro. In 2025 he has cashed 12 times at the WSOP, including two final tables and a monster‑stack win in a field of more than 10,000 players, with a single‑event win exceeding 1 million Euro, bringing his total earnings for the year to over 5 million Euro. Fellow Austrian Samuel Mullur also had a strong run in Barcelona, winning nearly 1 million Euro online on GGPoker in early August and then taking the 25,000‑Euro High Roller title for 327,000 Euro. Both players were eliminated on the first day of the 100,000‑Euro High Roller, but the tournament allows re‑entries until Sunday, leaving the outcome still open.

title: Year of the Grinder: Michael Mizrachi Wins 2025 WSOP Main Event, Hall of Fame Induction Caps Legendary Run – Better Poker News
content: Michael 'The Grinder' Mizrachi won the 2025 World Series of Poker (WSOP) Main Event, earning the biggest prize of his career and being inducted into the Poker Hall of Fame in the same year. The Main Event drew more than 12,000 entrants and created a prize pool of over $130 million. Mizrachi entered the final table as chip leader and won the heads‑up after a five‑hour battle with a full house, securing his first Main Event title. He now has over $35 million in live tournament earnings, multiple WSOP bracelets, and WPT titles. In his acceptance speech he said, 'For me, poker has always been about the grind,' and thanked his brothers Robert and Eric. Poker legend Daniel Negreanu tweeted, 'What a year! Mizrachi shows why he's one of the best ever. Main Event + Hall of Fame in one shot. Absolute legend!' The victory underscored the enduring appeal of live poker amid the rise of online platforms.

title: Poker-Talent Mullur räumt 920.000 Euro ab
content: Samuel Mullur, a young Austrian poker player from the Pokercode team, finished second in the 10,300 dollar GGMillions tournament on GGPoker, taking home 920,000 euros. Mullur, who has been a high roller in the poker scene for about 2.5 years, was sponsored by Fedor Holz, the founder of Pokercode, to play on higher levels. Mullur's breakthrough in the scene came when he won a 25,000 dollar tournament at the World Series of Poker Winter Edition on the Bahamas in 2023, taking home over 2 million euros. He has since played on the highest buy-in levels and has earned over 5.5 million euros in his career. Mullur is expected to participate in the World Series of Poker Europe in September, where he could win his first gold bracelet.

title: Ivan Deyra se régale online
content: French former Team Pro Winamax player Ivan Deyra won his third World Series of Poker (WSOP) bracelet in an online 10,000$ Heads‑Up No‑Limit Hold’em Championship on GGPoker. The event attracted 120 entrants and featured a demanding structure; Deyra, playing from his home in London, 'dominated' the tournament from start to finish. He earned $343,962 and a WSOP Paradise Super Pass worth $30,000. This is his third world title, following a 3,000$ NLH win in Las Vegas in 2019 ($380,090) and a 5,000$ 6‑Max Championship online in 2024 ($381,367). The win is described as a redemption for Deyra, who was expelled from Team Winamax in 2021 after a 'unforgivable act' involving a dual‑account scandal. The article reports the results factually, with no evident bias.

title: Martin Kabrhel et Shaun Deeb, 5ème et 8ème bracelet
content: At the WSOP Europe held at the King's Resort in Rozvadov, near the German border, two prominent international poker figures delivered standout performances. Martin Kabrhel, a well-known Czech player, won the $10,000 Pot-Limit Omaha Mystery Bounty event, defeating a field of 88 entrants to claim his 5th WSOP bracelet and a prize of €251,000. Known for his flamboyant style, Kabrhel entertained the table throughout the tournament. Meanwhile, American Shaun Deeb, recently crowned Player of the Year at the WSOP in Las Vegas, secured his 8th WSOP bracelet by winning the prestigious $25,000 NLH GGMillion€ event, defeating a strong field of 38 players and earning €329,000. The results were published on October 6, 2025, by RMC SPORT.
